image_spec.headline: Turkey still frozen? Cold water thaws it in about 30 minutes per pound.
image_spec.body: Keep it in its original wrapping, fully under cold water, and change the water every 30 minutes.
image_spec.tip: Cook it as soon as it's thawed.

posts.caption:
It's Wednesday night, you open the fridge, and the turkey is still a rock. It happens.

The USDA's fix is cold water. Leave the bird in its original wrapping, submerge it in cold water and plan on about 30 minutes per pound. Change the water every 30 minutes. A 14 pound turkey is roughly 7 hours. 🧊

Two rules. No thawing on the counter, and no hot water. Once it's thawed this way, it goes straight in the oven.

Send this to whoever's in charge of the turkey this year.

#smartshopping #groceryshopping #familymeals #stashsmart #mobilepantry
posts.source_note: USDA FSIS, Happy Thanksgiving (Thawing Turkey): cold water thawing, allow 30 minutes per pound, submerge in original wrapping, change the water every 30 minutes, cook immediately after thawing; thawing on the counter or in hot water is not safe. https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/poultry/happy-thanksgiving (14 lb x 30 min = 7 hours is our arithmetic)
